title: Tags, callouts and the / menu
highlights: Type / for lists, tables, callouts, dates and more.
Tag notes with #, and find them under Tags in the sidebar.
Link notes with [[Title]] and see what links back.
Pick a colour theme and an accent.
items: Type / at the start of a line to add a title, list, table, code block, callout, divider, date or file
Tags: write #work in a note to tag it. Tags in the sidebar lists them with counts, and #work/clients counts under #work
Callouts and highlights: coloured boxes with an icon and a title, the same format as Obsidian, and ==text== to highlight
Dates show as Today, Tomorrow or a weekday, and a click picks another day
Fold a section under its heading, and add divider lines from Format
Tables are easier to edit: taller rows, add bars and bigger handles
Colour themes (Paper, Sepia, Slate, Forest, High contrast) and an accent colour, in Settings, General, Appearance
Link to another note with [[Title]]. Each note lists what links to it, and renaming a note updates the links
Front matter and aliases survive import and export, and Export All Notes is in the File menu
Links on a line of their own show as a compact row or a card with a picture
Pictures fit the text's width, and can be small or a cover banner
Code blocks look like blocks, with the language in the corner
Notes use the full width, with Notes' heading weights and aligned list markers
Security shows who can open your notes, and the recovery key appears only when you need one
See every change an AI made across your notes
Settings as a card, a cleaner sidebar and top bar, and back and forward between notes
Shortcuts can create a note or add to one. Thanks to @sameer-dhande
Go to Note (⌘O) suggests notes and commands before you type, and signing in is one card over your notes

title: Pinto Notes
highlights: Amber Notes is now Pinto Notes. Same app, same notes, nothing to do.
Keep writing offline. Changes sync when you're back.
Files live in folders now, with PDF and picture viewers.
items: Amber Notes is now Pinto Notes. It's the same app with the same notes, and your AI connections keep working
On a Mac, the update renames the app to Pinto Notes. If you kept it in your Dock, drag Pinto Notes there again

If you downloaded the Mac app from our site, it asks for your key once after this update. Link the Mac from another device or type your recovery key, and Pinto Notes keeps the key on that Mac from then on. If you have neither, choose No device left? and Start fresh: the notes on your Mac are kept and uploaded again
Work offline: keep writing without a connection, and everything syncs when you're back
Files live in folders next to your notes, with 2 GB of storage and a Storage page in Settings
PDFs open in a viewer with zoom, drag-out and Export, and pictures open in a viewer of their own
HTML and code files open as code you can edit, with a Preview for HTML
Editing a file keeps its earlier versions
Settings is arranged in tabs
Connect an AI by scanning a QR code with your iPhone. No number to type
On a Mac, one click on the connect page opens Pinto Notes to allow it
The question is shorter: "Allow Claude to use your notes?", with read or edit access under Options
An AI's request stays in reach after you close its sheet, until you answer it
Every connected AI shows an icon and a name
A new leaf icon on iPhone and Mac
The app opens faster and uses no processor time while idle
Fixed: switching accounts could leave the other account's folders in the sidebar

title: Encrypted, end to end
highlights: Your notes are encrypted on your devices. We can't read them.
Approve an AI on your iPhone or Mac by typing the number your browser shows.
Import from Evernote, Google Keep and Markdown files.
Connect your AI apps once more after this update.
items: Every note, folder, file and earlier version is encrypted on your devices. We can't read them
Your key syncs through iCloud Keychain, so your notes open on your other devices with nothing to type
Save a recovery key in Settings › Privacy & Security, for when none of your devices is nearby
Approve an AI on your iPhone or Mac: type the two-digit number your browser shows
Each device shows a notice when an AI connects, with Disconnect
Get a notification on your iPhone or Mac when an AI asks to connect
Export your notes as Markdown from Settings › Privacy & Security
Import from Evernote, Google Keep, or Markdown and text files (Obsidian, Notion, Bear and more), with folders, checklists and attachments
One Import Notes button on the setup card, for Apple Notes and the rest
Use a template from pintonotes.com/templates and it opens in Amber Notes, ready to add to a folder
"Use this note" on a shared note copies it into your own notes
After updating, connect your AI apps once more

title: Hello, Amber Notes
items: Notes, folders, checklists that tidy themselves, tables, photos and files
Connect ChatGPT or Claude so they can read and update your notes, with your approval
Changes show on your Mac and iPhone in about a second
Share a note as a web page, and stop sharing whenever you like
Import your notes from Apple Notes
Sign in with Apple or email
